sentences.text: Partly from surveys: one study measured maintainability and technical debt through its respondents' answers to questionnaire scales, and AI use went with lower maintainability and more debt.
That is an association in people's answers, not a timed test of someone else changing the code.

sentences.text: Then there is code out in the wild: a study that tracked commits made with AI coding assistants found that some of the issues they introduced still survive in the latest code.

onScreenText: Some issues still survive in the latest code

sentences.text: The assistants fixed about as many code smells, surface problems like naming and formatting, as they introduced; but they introduced more correctness and security issues than they fixed.

excerpt.text:
findings suggest that although AI coding assistants introduce technical debt, they also fix existing
issues in the codebase. First, we observe that AI co-authored commits actually fix a similar number
of code smell issues as they introduce. This suggests that AI coding assistants are able to perform
local cleanup and repetitive maintenance tasks effectively. They can recognize and address surface-
level code quality problems (e.g., formatting, naming, or simple refactoring opportunities). However,
what is concerning is that AI coding assistants seem to be less effective at fixing correctness and
security issues, and they even introduce more of these than they fix. Section 5.3 shows that many
AI-introduced issues still survive at HEAD, while the net-impact analysis shows that AI commits
introduce more correctness and security issues than they fix. This inconsistency suggests that
AI coding assistants may struggle with changes that require a deeper understanding of program
behavior, execution context, or security implications. Also, the practical impact of correctness and
security issues is often more severe than that of code smells, making it more critical to address
them effectively. Developers should not treat all AI-generated code as equally trustworthy, and they
should pay particular attention to changes that may introduce correctness or security vulnerabilities.

   Technical debt cannot be solved by switching between AI coding tools. Our cross-tool
excerpt.highlight: introduce more correctness and security issues than they fix

citations.label: Study of AI co-authored commits, net impact

sentences.text: But the authors did not compare those commits with code written by people alone, so the study cannot say AI code leaves more debt than human code does.

excerpt.text:
We also do not compare AI-authored commits against a baseline of purely human-written commits.
Because developers may use AI without leaving any Git trace, and even AI-labeled commits may
mix human edits, a reliable human-only baseline is difficult to construct, and comparing against
an unreliable baseline could bias the results. We therefore focus on tracking technical debt inside
explicitly confirmed AI-authored or co-authored commits.
excerpt.highlight: We also do not compare AI-authored commits against a baseline of purely human-written commits.

sentences.text: And the security worry? One study did put a number on it: of 733 code snippets generated by AI, 27.3 percent contained security weaknesses.
That is a count of weaknesses in AI code alone; it cannot tell you whether code written by hand would score any better on the same check.

sentences.text: There is one cost, though, that experiments did measure, and it lands on the person who wrote the code.

In one trial, crowd workers recruited online, most of them freelance or professional software developers, did a coding task with or without AI, then took a quiz on the skills the task should have built.

onScreenText: A coding task with or without AI, then a quiz

sentences.text: Using AI did not make them significantly faster, and their scores came out lower by a gap worth 17 percent of the quiz.

chart.title: Quiz score gap with AI

points.label: Lower score, share of the quiz

chart.note: Completion time was not significantly faster with AI.

sentences.text: In a separate experiment with different participants, working with AI cut their chance of answering questions about their own code correctly by 5.95 percentage points.
The authors re-checked it other ways: each time the drop kept its direction, though in one it was too weak to be sure of.

chart.title: Answering questions about their own code correctly, with AI
chart.note: Percentage points, not percent; direction held in every re-check.

sentences.text: So, is AI-written code harder to maintain? In the one trial that tested it, over the time it ran, no: no reliable difference in speed or code health, though one trial with that much uncertainty cannot rule out a small one.
